definition: Calibrating a strike or reach's extreme pose by placing a stand-in target object just out of the character's comfortable reach, then pushing every available joint (spine twist, clavicle, arm stretch/extension) toward it until the pose is close to breaking, rather than choosing the extreme pose's exact extent by eye alone - the placeholder target is deleted or ignored once its job (calibrating how far the pose can plausibly go) is done.
purpose: Give a reach or strike's most extreme pose an objective, checkable target to push against, instead of a distance chosen purely by visual judgement with nothing to verify it against.
visible_effect: The extreme pose visibly uses every available joint to close the last part of the distance to the target (a spine twist, a clavicle push, a fully stretched arm) rather than stopping short with an under-extended pose, or breaking the rig by reaching past what those joints can plausibly cover.
psychological_or_gameplay_effect: A pose visibly pushed to its plausible limit reads as more committed and powerful than one that stops at a comfortable, un-stressed extension - the video frames this explicitly as turning a weak first pass into 'a much stronger punch pose'.
physical_interpretation: A real strike is thrown to actually connect with a target at a specific distance, so a pose calibrated against a placeholder at that same distance is closer to what the joints would really have to do than a pose chosen with no target distance in mind at all.
use_cases: any strike, reach, or grab whose extreme pose's exact extent matters (does the hand plausibly reach the target, and how much of the body has to contort to get there)
diagnosing why an extreme pose reads as insufficiently committed - checking it against an explicit target distance rather than adjusting it by eye alone
non_use_cases: a pose with no specific spatial target to reach for (a non-contact gesture, an idle) where there is nothing meaningful to calibrate against
a final production pass where the placeholder's job is already done and an explicit contact/IK target (not a throwaway placeholder) should be used instead
interactions: structural_understanding / appeal - the resulting pose's balance and line of action are exactly what those cards already discuss measuring; this entry is about HOW the pose's raw extent gets decided in the first place, upstream of judging the result

solve_ik / compute_swing_twist (existing Cadence tools) - a placeholder target used this way is conceptually the same thing an IK target already is in Cadence; the video's version is a manual, iterative, by-eye process rather than a single solve
cadence_representation: Partially reachable, through a different route than the source's manual process: Cadence already has `solve_ik` (analytic two-bone IK onto a target in studs) and `compute_swing_twist`, which could place an effector exactly at a declared target position directly rather than iteratively nudging a pose toward one by eye - but nothing currently reports whether a solved reach is NEAR the rig's own limit (close to breaking, in the video's own words) versus comfortably within it, which is the specific judgement the video's manual push-toward-the-target process is making at each step.
control_surface: `solve_ik` already solves an effector onto a declared target; nothing reports margin-to-limit for the result.
detection_and_measurement_methods: Partially real: CLAUDE.md's own documented reach-limit facts (e.g. an R15 leg chain's exact 1.85-stud maximum, an arm's 1.6888-stud maximum) mean a solved reach's distance from its declared target, and its distance from the chain's own known maximum, are BOTH already computable numbers - what is not built is reporting the second one (how close to breaking a given reach pose is) as a named result a caller would see.
generation_or_modification_methods: `solve_ik` already generates a reach pose onto a declared target in one solve; the video's manual, iterative joint-by-joint push (twist first, then clavicle, then arm stretch) toward a target is a different, exploratory process this build does not need to replicate once a target is declared, since the analytic solve already exists.
failure_modes: choosing an extreme pose's reach distance with no target to check it against, leaving it either under-committed or past what the rig can plausibly cover
leaving a placeholder target object in the final data after its calibration job is done, rather than replacing it with a real declared contact or IK target
roblox_considerations: None beyond the existing rig/IK model - Roblox's own IK API can solve onto a declared world target the same way `solve_ik` does.
examples: "I will create an object for the character to punch... put it just out of his reach and I will try to push this pose to see how far I can get this character to reach forward before I start to break it... just by twisting his body... maybe I would also use the clavicle push that a little bit more... if I have some options to stretch this arm maybe I would even consider doing that" (video @ 04:58-05:33)
evidence_status: video: https://youtu.be/tcBT-6wdSC8 @ 04:58-05:33 - Greg Marlow describes and performs this calibration process live while posing the punch in a Maya viewport; no frame in this session's 9-frame sample falls in this exact window (nearest sampled frames are at t=03:43 and t=03:43, before this passage), so this rests on the transcript's specific, concrete description rather than a directly-viewed pose; experimental until validated
